Sentence (English): Product Features.
Comments (English): Product Features. The Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Countertop 6-Place Dishwasher is a 6-place dishwasher featuring the BESPOKE design. Its basic functions include various cycles such as Eco, Powerful, Quick, Sterilization, Schedule, Add during wash, and High Temperature Sterilization. Additionally, it allows for thorough cleaning through its three-dimensional water jets with upper and lower wings. User Review. I am in a household of three, and I have been using the dishwasher for about four months. First of all, I really like the design. The clean white color blends well with the interior. The cleaning power is also satisfactory. Even greasy dishes are cleaned thoroughly. In particular, using the 'Sterilization' cycle completely removes stubborn stains and bacteria. The noise level is also not noticeable. While there is some noise during the wash cycle, it is quiet enough to be masked by everyday noise. Overall, I consider it a satisfactory product. Sentence (English): We've owned Bosch dishwashers for nearly 20 years and wouldn't get anything else.
Comments (English): [ Great machine, but a couple of disappointments. ] || ---------------- || We've owned Bosch dishwashers for nearly 20 years and wouldn't get anything else. We love almost everything about this one - the AutoAir feature is fantastic a simple but ingenious idea to facilitate drying at the end of the cycle. The 3rd upper rack is great as is the full stainless steel tub. There are two downsides. The biggest is that (and this is from the Bosch website) the "Touch Controls respond to the lightest touch. Touch controls are responsive, offering easy cycle and option programming at the lightest touch." That means that at least once a day, I accidentally activate the controls. The machine beeps at me and I must turn it off. I wish we'd purchased the version with the bar handle. The other disappointment is the silverware basket - it's small, awkward and not configurable. We purchased the upgrade for ~$40 (incl. shipping). For a $1K machine, Bosch should include the better one. Otherwise, it works like a charm and we love it.

Comments (English): I'll leave a review as soon as I get it. I carefully looked at other reviews and bought it. Price First, the price on Coupang fluctuates a lot. I didn't know at first, so I bought it, but when I read the reviews, they said it fluctuated a lot, so I went back the next day and it was 50,000 won cheaper? So I immediately requested a cancellation and barely saved 50,000 won by repurchasing it. Installation I was a little worried because there were a lot of stories about the installer, but he was kind and the installation took about 40 minutes. There was a hole for the water purifier, so he connected the line to that side and did it very thoroughly. I washed it right after he left. I'm not sure about the cleaning power, but the plastic was cleaned thoroughly. Noise Some people said the noise was worse than expected, but it's about the same level as a washing machine. I expected the noise, so it wasn't too uncomfortable. Drying I saw a few articles saying that it didn't dry well, but since this is my first time using a dishwasher, I don't know if this is true, but it didn't dry well. It was partially dried, so I think I need to watch this part a little more. Is it because I didn't put in a separate rinse? But anyway? Even if I wash it by hand, there will still be moisture left, so I'll just take it out and let it dry. Since the door opens automatically anyway, I think I can wait a little longer. LG induction cooktops can be installed if they're 75mm above the dishwasher. You'll need to look into other models separately. The installation was very neat and beautiful. Comments (English): [ Great dishwasher ] || ---------------- || We only purchased this dishwasher on the weekend so the ownership time frame has been less than a week. We are a family of 5 so we are heavy users of our appliances, and our dishwasher is on daily. This dishwasher was the first built in that we have had and I was reluctant to drill screws into our kitchen. The fitment was relatively simple with a thought out system for leg adjustment front and rear. The dishwasher was significantly lighter than our old free standing unit as it doesn't require in built weight to stop the whole thing from tilting forward when the draw slides out onto the door with the added weight of dishes. The fixed nature of the built in unit(as it is screwed in) holds it in place, this means that the lower draw can slide further out onto the door allowing better access to the top and bottom rack at the same time. The racks have a quality feel to them which sounds odd but try them out in store, they slide a lot easier on what feels like ball bearing slides. The small screen offers more detail than I expected and the simple wash programs are enough for what we need. The pop-open door feature at the end of the wash helps everything to dry off and cool down before emptying. The dishwasher has plenty of space for our needs. Great unit that surprised and I would recommend to any busy family.

Comments (English): [ The installers are always friendly ] || ---------------- || It arrived and was installed in just two days. I don't usually write reviews, but I felt I had to this time. This is also the reason I deducted one star. I had the same model Samsung dishwasher installed in October 2023 and used it well for nearly three months. However, starting around the end of December, detergent powder started appearing on the dishes and inside the dishwasher (I have attached a photo below), so I requested an after-sales service. The technician came, inspected it, and confirmed it was detergent powder. He told me to reduce the amount of detergent used (as shown in the photo, half the original amount was being used). When I said I was using less, he told me to use rinse aid instead. I was already using rinse aid. He suggested I try changing the detergent, specifically liquid detergent instead of solid detergent. However, the problem persists even after switching. The same issue occurred with the SK 3-place setting detergent I used before switching to solid detergent. Doesn't that imply a problem with the dishwasher? He claims there is nothing wrong because the dishwasher is working properly. He told me to call him if the issue persists even after changing the detergent and running it on the "Powerful" setting. I called the technician and sent him photos saying the problem was exactly the same. He then told me to send a video showing the white substance forming inside the dishwasher and to get a water quality check. I don't understand. If he had said that from the beginning, I would have assumed it was a problem with the minerals or the composition of the tap water, as he claimed. However, it used to clean perfectly well before. I asked the apartment complex, and they said they haven't had any water inspections or replacements since September. Despite this, the technician claimed that the phenomenon is caused by the temperature difference between the tap water and detergent components, and told me to use something like a water purifier filter at the water outlet if it bothered me too much. When I asked if he was crazy and why I would use the dishwasher like that, he insisted it wasn't defective and tried to teach me about water purification. Furious, I called another technician. He said the same thing. In the end, I told him to take the dishwasher away because I couldn't use it. The second technician said he would have the customer service center report how the previous technician acted and would look into a refund without further ado, but he left with the possibility that it might not work out. He said he would pass on the message to the company's top manager demanding a refund, and if that worked, he would issue it. The next day, I received a call asking me to send a photo of the receipt. I attached five photos and sent a picture of the receipt, and they said they would issue a refund, so I received it. The reasons I purchased the same model again are: 1. The price is reasonable. 2. It was convenient to use as the cutlery holder is located at the front. 3. Since I had been using it, I was used to it and didn't want to switch to a different model. 4. I bought the same model again with the intention of just using it if the problem occurred again. 5. Looking at dishwasher reviews, Samsung products are said to be the best (I previously replaced my SK 3-place setting model because it was too small). I am hoping that this issue won't happen this time.

Comments (English): [ The installers are always friendly ] || ---------------- || It arrived and was installed in just two days. I don't usually write reviews, but I felt I had to this time. This is also the reason I deducted one star. I had the same model Samsung dishwasher installed in October 2023 and used it well for nearly three months. However, starting around the end of December, detergent powder started appearing on the dishes and inside the dishwasher (I have attached a photo below), so I requested an after-sales service. The technician came, inspected it, and confirmed it was detergent powder. He told me to reduce the amount of detergent used (as shown in the photo, half the original amount was being used). When I said I was using less, he told me to use rinse aid instead. I was already using rinse aid. He suggested I try changing the detergent, specifically liquid detergent instead of solid detergent. However, the problem persists even after switching. The same issue occurred with the SK 3-place setting detergent I used before switching to solid detergent. Doesn't that imply a problem with the dishwasher? He claims there is nothing wrong because the dishwasher is working properly. He told me to call him if the issue persists even after changing the detergent and running it on the "Powerful" setting. I called the technician and sent him photos saying the problem was exactly the same. He then told me to send a video showing the white substance forming inside the dishwasher and to get a water quality check. I don't understand. If he had said that from the beginning, I would have assumed it was a problem with the minerals or the composition of the tap water, as he claimed. However, it used to clean perfectly well before. I asked the apartment complex, and they said they haven't had any water inspections or replacements since September. Despite this, the technician claimed that the phenomenon is caused by the temperature difference between the tap water and detergent components, and told me to use something like a water purifier filter at the water outlet if it bothered me too much. When I asked if he was crazy and why I would use the dishwasher like that, he insisted it wasn't defective and tried to teach me about water purification. Furious, I called another technician. He said the same thing. In the end, I told him to take the dishwasher away because I couldn't use it. The second technician said he would have the customer service center report how the previous technician acted and would look into a refund without further ado, but he left with the possibility that it might not work out. He said he would pass on the message to the company's top manager demanding a refund, and if that worked, he would issue it. The next day, I received a call asking me to send a photo of the receipt. I attached five photos and sent a picture of the receipt, and they said they would issue a refund, so I received it. The reasons I purchased the same model again are: 1. The price is reasonable. 2. It was convenient to use as the cutlery holder is located at the front. 3. Since I had been using it, I was used to it and didn't want to switch to a different model. 4. I bought the same model again with the intention of just using it if the problem occurred again. 5. Looking at dishwasher reviews, Samsung products are said to be the best (I previously replaced my SK 3-place setting model because it was too small). I am hoping that this issue won't happen this time.

Sentence (English): The technician came, inspected it, and confirmed it was detergent powder.
Comments (English): [ The installers are always friendly ] || ---------------- || It arrived and was installed in just two days. I don't usually write reviews, but I felt I had to this time. This is also the reason I deducted one star. I had the same model Samsung dishwasher installed in October 2023 and used it well for nearly three months. However, starting around the end of December, detergent powder started appearing on the dishes and inside the dishwasher (I have attached a photo below), so I requested an after-sales service. The technician came, inspected it, and confirmed it was detergent powder. He told me to reduce the amount of detergent used (as shown in the photo, half the original amount was being used). When I said I was using less, he told me to use rinse aid instead. I was already using rinse aid. He suggested I try changing the detergent, specifically liquid detergent instead of solid detergent. However, the problem persists even after switching. The same issue occurred with the SK 3-place setting detergent I used before switching to solid detergent. Doesn't that imply a problem with the dishwasher? He claims there is nothing wrong because the dishwasher is working properly. He told me to call him if the issue persists even after changing the detergent and running it on the "Powerful" setting. I called the technician and sent him photos saying the problem was exactly the same. He then told me to send a video showing the white substance forming inside the dishwasher and to get a water quality check. I don't understand. If he had said that from the beginning, I would have assumed it was a problem with the minerals or the composition of the tap water, as he claimed. However, it used to clean perfectly well before. I asked the apartment complex, and they said they haven't had any water inspections or replacements since September. Despite this, the technician claimed that the phenomenon is caused by the temperature difference between the tap water and detergent components, and told me to use something like a water purifier filter at the water outlet if it bothered me too much. When I asked if he was crazy and why I would use the dishwasher like that, he insisted it wasn't defective and tried to teach me about water purification. Furious, I called another technician. He said the same thing. In the end, I told him to take the dishwasher away because I couldn't use it. The second technician said he would have the customer service center report how the previous technician acted and would look into a refund without further ado, but he left with the possibility that it might not work out. He said he would pass on the message to the company's top manager demanding a refund, and if that worked, he would issue it. The next day, I received a call asking me to send a photo of the receipt. I attached five photos and sent a picture of the receipt, and they said they would issue a refund, so I received it. The reasons I purchased the same model again are: 1. The price is reasonable. 2. It was convenient to use as the cutlery holder is located at the front. 3. Since I had been using it, I was used to it and didn't want to switch to a different model. 4. I bought the same model again with the intention of just using it if the problem occurred again. 5. Looking at dishwasher reviews, Samsung products are said to be the best (I previously replaced my SK 3-place setting model because it was too small). I am hoping that this issue won't happen this time.

Sentence (English): I was already using rinse aid.
Comments (English): [ The installers are always friendly ] || ---------------- || It arrived and was installed in just two days. I don't usually write reviews, but I felt I had to this time. This is also the reason I deducted one star. I had the same model Samsung dishwasher installed in October 2023 and used it well for nearly three months. However, starting around the end of December, detergent powder started appearing on the dishes and inside the dishwasher (I have attached a photo below), so I requested an after-sales service. The technician came, inspected it, and confirmed it was detergent powder. He told me to reduce the amount of detergent used (as shown in the photo, half the original amount was being used). When I said I was using less, he told me to use rinse aid instead. I was already using rinse aid. He suggested I try changing the detergent, specifically liquid detergent instead of solid detergent. However, the problem persists even after switching. The same issue occurred with the SK 3-place setting detergent I used before switching to solid detergent. Doesn't that imply a problem with the dishwasher? He claims there is nothing wrong because the dishwasher is working properly. He told me to call him if the issue persists even after changing the detergent and running it on the "Powerful" setting. I called the technician and sent him photos saying the problem was exactly the same. He then told me to send a video showing the white substance forming inside the dishwasher and to get a water quality check. I don't understand. If he had said that from the beginning, I would have assumed it was a problem with the minerals or the composition of the tap water, as he claimed. However, it used to clean perfectly well before. I asked the apartment complex, and they said they haven't had any water inspections or replacements since September. Despite this, the technician claimed that the phenomenon is caused by the temperature difference between the tap water and detergent components, and told me to use something like a water purifier filter at the water outlet if it bothered me too much. When I asked if he was crazy and why I would use the dishwasher like that, he insisted it wasn't defective and tried to teach me about water purification. Furious, I called another technician. He said the same thing. In the end, I told him to take the dishwasher away because I couldn't use it. The second technician said he would have the customer service center report how the previous technician acted and would look into a refund without further ado, but he left with the possibility that it might not work out. He said he would pass on the message to the company's top manager demanding a refund, and if that worked, he would issue it. The next day, I received a call asking me to send a photo of the receipt. I attached five photos and sent a picture of the receipt, and they said they would issue a refund, so I received it. The reasons I purchased the same model again are: 1. The price is reasonable. 2. It was convenient to use as the cutlery holder is located at the front. 3. Since I had been using it, I was used to it and didn't want to switch to a different model. 4. I bought the same model again with the intention of just using it if the problem occurred again. 5. Looking at dishwasher reviews, Samsung products are said to be the best (I previously replaced my SK 3-place setting model because it was too small). I am hoping that this issue won't happen this time.

Sentence (English): The same issue occurred with the SK 3-place setting detergent I used before switching to solid detergent.
Comments (English): [ The installers are always friendly ] || ---------------- || It arrived and was installed in just two days. I don't usually write reviews, but I felt I had to this time. This is also the reason I deducted one star. I had the same model Samsung dishwasher installed in October 2023 and used it well for nearly three months. However, starting around the end of December, detergent powder started appearing on the dishes and inside the dishwasher (I have attached a photo below), so I requested an after-sales service. The technician came, inspected it, and confirmed it was detergent powder. He told me to reduce the amount of detergent used (as shown in the photo, half the original amount was being used). When I said I was using less, he told me to use rinse aid instead. I was already using rinse aid. He suggested I try changing the detergent, specifically liquid detergent instead of solid detergent. However, the problem persists even after switching. The same issue occurred with the SK 3-place setting detergent I used before switching to solid detergent. Doesn't that imply a problem with the dishwasher? He claims there is nothing wrong because the dishwasher is working properly. He told me to call him if the issue persists even after changing the detergent and running it on the "Powerful" setting. I called the technician and sent him photos saying the problem was exactly the same. He then told me to send a video showing the white substance forming inside the dishwasher and to get a water quality check. I don't understand. If he had said that from the beginning, I would have assumed it was a problem with the minerals or the composition of the tap water, as he claimed. However, it used to clean perfectly well before. I asked the apartment complex, and they said they haven't had any water inspections or replacements since September. Despite this, the technician claimed that the phenomenon is caused by the temperature difference between the tap water and detergent components, and told me to use something like a water purifier filter at the water outlet if it bothered me too much. When I asked if he was crazy and why I would use the dishwasher like that, he insisted it wasn't defective and tried to teach me about water purification. Furious, I called another technician. He said the same thing. In the end, I told him to take the dishwasher away because I couldn't use it. The second technician said he would have the customer service center report how the previous technician acted and would look into a refund without further ado, but he left with the possibility that it might not work out. He said he would pass on the message to the company's top manager demanding a refund, and if that worked, he would issue it. The next day, I received a call asking me to send a photo of the receipt. I attached five photos and sent a picture of the receipt, and they said they would issue a refund, so I received it. The reasons I purchased the same model again are: 1. The price is reasonable. 2. It was convenient to use as the cutlery holder is located at the front. 3. Since I had been using it, I was used to it and didn't want to switch to a different model. 4. I bought the same model again with the intention of just using it if the problem occurred again. 5. Looking at dishwasher reviews, Samsung products are said to be the best (I previously replaced my SK 3-place setting model because it was too small). I am hoping that this issue won't happen this time.

Comments (English): [ The installers are always friendly ] || ---------------- || It arrived and was installed in just two days. I don't usually write reviews, but I felt I had to this time. This is also the reason I deducted one star. I had the same model Samsung dishwasher installed in October 2023 and used it well for nearly three months. However, starting around the end of December, detergent powder started appearing on the dishes and inside the dishwasher (I have attached a photo below), so I requested an after-sales service. The technician came, inspected it, and confirmed it was detergent powder. He told me to reduce the amount of detergent used (as shown in the photo, half the original amount was being used). When I said I was using less, he told me to use rinse aid instead. I was already using rinse aid. He suggested I try changing the detergent, specifically liquid detergent instead of solid detergent. However, the problem persists even after switching. The same issue occurred with the SK 3-place setting detergent I used before switching to solid detergent. Doesn't that imply a problem with the dishwasher? He claims there is nothing wrong because the dishwasher is working properly. He told me to call him if the issue persists even after changing the detergent and running it on the "Powerful" setting. I called the technician and sent him photos saying the problem was exactly the same. He then told me to send a video showing the white substance forming inside the dishwasher and to get a water quality check. I don't understand. If he had said that from the beginning, I would have assumed it was a problem with the minerals or the composition of the tap water, as he claimed. However, it used to clean perfectly well before. I asked the apartment complex, and they said they haven't had any water inspections or replacements since September. Despite this, the technician claimed that the phenomenon is caused by the temperature difference between the tap water and detergent components, and told me to use something like a water purifier filter at the water outlet if it bothered me too much. When I asked if he was crazy and why I would use the dishwasher like that, he insisted it wasn't defective and tried to teach me about water purification. Furious, I called another technician. He said the same thing. In the end, I told him to take the dishwasher away because I couldn't use it. The second technician said he would have the customer service center report how the previous technician acted and would look into a refund without further ado, but he left with the possibility that it might not work out. He said he would pass on the message to the company's top manager demanding a refund, and if that worked, he would issue it. The next day, I received a call asking me to send a photo of the receipt. I attached five photos and sent a picture of the receipt, and they said they would issue a refund, so I received it. The reasons I purchased the same model again are: 1. The price is reasonable. 2. It was convenient to use as the cutlery holder is located at the front. 3. Since I had been using it, I was used to it and didn't want to switch to a different model. 4. I bought the same model again with the intention of just using it if the problem occurred again. 5. Looking at dishwasher reviews, Samsung products are said to be the best (I previously replaced my SK 3-place setting model because it was too small). I am hoping that this issue won't happen this time.

Sentence (English): I don't understand.
Comments (English): [ The installers are always friendly ] || ---------------- || It arrived and was installed in just two days. I don't usually write reviews, but I felt I had to this time. This is also the reason I deducted one star. I had the same model Samsung dishwasher installed in October 2023 and used it well for nearly three months. However, starting around the end of December, detergent powder started appearing on the dishes and inside the dishwasher (I have attached a photo below), so I requested an after-sales service. The technician came, inspected it, and confirmed it was detergent powder. He told me to reduce the amount of detergent used (as shown in the photo, half the original amount was being used). When I said I was using less, he told me to use rinse aid instead. I was already using rinse aid. He suggested I try changing the detergent, specifically liquid detergent instead of solid detergent. However, the problem persists even after switching. The same issue occurred with the SK 3-place setting detergent I used before switching to solid detergent. Doesn't that imply a problem with the dishwasher? He claims there is nothing wrong because the dishwasher is working properly. He told me to call him if the issue persists even after changing the detergent and running it on the "Powerful" setting. I called the technician and sent him photos saying the problem was exactly the same. He then told me to send a video showing the white substance forming inside the dishwasher and to get a water quality check. I don't understand. If he had said that from the beginning, I would have assumed it was a problem with the minerals or the composition of the tap water, as he claimed. However, it used to clean perfectly well before. I asked the apartment complex, and they said they haven't had any water inspections or replacements since September. Despite this, the technician claimed that the phenomenon is caused by the temperature difference between the tap water and detergent components, and told me to use something like a water purifier filter at the water outlet if it bothered me too much. When I asked if he was crazy and why I would use the dishwasher like that, he insisted it wasn't defective and tried to teach me about water purification. Furious, I called another technician. He said the same thing. In the end, I told him to take the dishwasher away because I couldn't use it. The second technician said he would have the customer service center report how the previous technician acted and would look into a refund without further ado, but he left with the possibility that it might not work out. He said he would pass on the message to the company's top manager demanding a refund, and if that worked, he would issue it. The next day, I received a call asking me to send a photo of the receipt. I attached five photos and sent a picture of the receipt, and they said they would issue a refund, so I received it. The reasons I purchased the same model again are: 1. The price is reasonable. 2. It was convenient to use as the cutlery holder is located at the front. 3. Since I had been using it, I was used to it and didn't want to switch to a different model. 4. I bought the same model again with the intention of just using it if the problem occurred again. 5. Looking at dishwasher reviews, Samsung products are said to be the best (I previously replaced my SK 3-place setting model because it was too small). I am hoping that this issue won't happen this time.

Comments (English): [ The installers are always friendly ] || ---------------- || It arrived and was installed in just two days. I don't usually write reviews, but I felt I had to this time. This is also the reason I deducted one star. I had the same model Samsung dishwasher installed in October 2023 and used it well for nearly three months. However, starting around the end of December, detergent powder started appearing on the dishes and inside the dishwasher (I have attached a photo below), so I requested an after-sales service. The technician came, inspected it, and confirmed it was detergent powder. He told me to reduce the amount of detergent used (as shown in the photo, half the original amount was being used). When I said I was using less, he told me to use rinse aid instead. I was already using rinse aid. He suggested I try changing the detergent, specifically liquid detergent instead of solid detergent. However, the problem persists even after switching. The same issue occurred with the SK 3-place setting detergent I used before switching to solid detergent. Doesn't that imply a problem with the dishwasher? He claims there is nothing wrong because the dishwasher is working properly. He told me to call him if the issue persists even after changing the detergent and running it on the "Powerful" setting. I called the technician and sent him photos saying the problem was exactly the same. He then told me to send a video showing the white substance forming inside the dishwasher and to get a water quality check. I don't understand. If he had said that from the beginning, I would have assumed it was a problem with the minerals or the composition of the tap water, as he claimed. However, it used to clean perfectly well before. I asked the apartment complex, and they said they haven't had any water inspections or replacements since September. Despite this, the technician claimed that the phenomenon is caused by the temperature difference between the tap water and detergent components, and told me to use something like a water purifier filter at the water outlet if it bothered me too much. When I asked if he was crazy and why I would use the dishwasher like that, he insisted it wasn't defective and tried to teach me about water purification. Furious, I called another technician. He said the same thing. In the end, I told him to take the dishwasher away because I couldn't use it. The second technician said he would have the customer service center report how the previous technician acted and would look into a refund without further ado, but he left with the possibility that it might not work out. He said he would pass on the message to the company's top manager demanding a refund, and if that worked, he would issue it. The next day, I received a call asking me to send a photo of the receipt. I attached five photos and sent a picture of the receipt, and they said they would issue a refund, so I received it. The reasons I purchased the same model again are: 1. The price is reasonable. 2. It was convenient to use as the cutlery holder is located at the front. 3. Since I had been using it, I was used to it and didn't want to switch to a different model. 4. I bought the same model again with the intention of just using it if the problem occurred again. 5. Looking at dishwasher reviews, Samsung products are said to be the best (I previously replaced my SK 3-place setting model because it was too small). I am hoping that this issue won't happen this time.

Sentence (English): Furious, I called another technician.
Comments (English): [ The installers are always friendly ] || ---------------- || It arrived and was installed in just two days. I don't usually write reviews, but I felt I had to this time. This is also the reason I deducted one star. I had the same model Samsung dishwasher installed in October 2023 and used it well for nearly three months. However, starting around the end of December, detergent powder started appearing on the dishes and inside the dishwasher (I have attached a photo below), so I requested an after-sales service. The technician came, inspected it, and confirmed it was detergent powder. He told me to reduce the amount of detergent used (as shown in the photo, half the original amount was being used). When I said I was using less, he told me to use rinse aid instead. I was already using rinse aid. He suggested I try changing the detergent, specifically liquid detergent instead of solid detergent. However, the problem persists even after switching. The same issue occurred with the SK 3-place setting detergent I used before switching to solid detergent. Doesn't that imply a problem with the dishwasher? He claims there is nothing wrong because the dishwasher is working properly. He told me to call him if the issue persists even after changing the detergent and running it on the "Powerful" setting. I called the technician and sent him photos saying the problem was exactly the same. He then told me to send a video showing the white substance forming inside the dishwasher and to get a water quality check. I don't understand. If he had said that from the beginning, I would have assumed it was a problem with the minerals or the composition of the tap water, as he claimed. However, it used to clean perfectly well before. I asked the apartment complex, and they said they haven't had any water inspections or replacements since September. Despite this, the technician claimed that the phenomenon is caused by the temperature difference between the tap water and detergent components, and told me to use something like a water purifier filter at the water outlet if it bothered me too much. When I asked if he was crazy and why I would use the dishwasher like that, he insisted it wasn't defective and tried to teach me about water purification. Furious, I called another technician. He said the same thing. In the end, I told him to take the dishwasher away because I couldn't use it. The second technician said he would have the customer service center report how the previous technician acted and would look into a refund without further ado, but he left with the possibility that it might not work out. He said he would pass on the message to the company's top manager demanding a refund, and if that worked, he would issue it. The next day, I received a call asking me to send a photo of the receipt. I attached five photos and sent a picture of the receipt, and they said they would issue a refund, so I received it. The reasons I purchased the same model again are: 1. The price is reasonable. 2. It was convenient to use as the cutlery holder is located at the front. 3. Since I had been using it, I was used to it and didn't want to switch to a different model. 4. I bought the same model again with the intention of just using it if the problem occurred again. 5. Looking at dishwasher reviews, Samsung products are said to be the best (I previously replaced my SK 3-place setting model because it was too small). I am hoping that this issue won't happen this time.

Comments (English): [ The installers are always friendly ] || ---------------- || It arrived and was installed in just two days. I don't usually write reviews, but I felt I had to this time. This is also the reason I deducted one star. I had the same model Samsung dishwasher installed in October 2023 and used it well for nearly three months. However, starting around the end of December, detergent powder started appearing on the dishes and inside the dishwasher (I have attached a photo below), so I requested an after-sales service. The technician came, inspected it, and confirmed it was detergent powder. He told me to reduce the amount of detergent used (as shown in the photo, half the original amount was being used). When I said I was using less, he told me to use rinse aid instead. I was already using rinse aid. He suggested I try changing the detergent, specifically liquid detergent instead of solid detergent. However, the problem persists even after switching. The same issue occurred with the SK 3-place setting detergent I used before switching to solid detergent. Doesn't that imply a problem with the dishwasher? He claims there is nothing wrong because the dishwasher is working properly. He told me to call him if the issue persists even after changing the detergent and running it on the "Powerful" setting. I called the technician and sent him photos saying the problem was exactly the same. He then told me to send a video showing the white substance forming inside the dishwasher and to get a water quality check. I don't understand. If he had said that from the beginning, I would have assumed it was a problem with the minerals or the composition of the tap water, as he claimed. However, it used to clean perfectly well before. I asked the apartment complex, and they said they haven't had any water inspections or replacements since September. Despite this, the technician claimed that the phenomenon is caused by the temperature difference between the tap water and detergent components, and told me to use something like a water purifier filter at the water outlet if it bothered me too much. When I asked if he was crazy and why I would use the dishwasher like that, he insisted it wasn't defective and tried to teach me about water purification. Furious, I called another technician. He said the same thing. In the end, I told him to take the dishwasher away because I couldn't use it. The second technician said he would have the customer service center report how the previous technician acted and would look into a refund without further ado, but he left with the possibility that it might not work out. He said he would pass on the message to the company's top manager demanding a refund, and if that worked, he would issue it. The next day, I received a call asking me to send a photo of the receipt. I attached five photos and sent a picture of the receipt, and they said they would issue a refund, so I received it. The reasons I purchased the same model again are: 1. The price is reasonable. 2. It was convenient to use as the cutlery holder is located at the front. 3. Since I had been using it, I was used to it and didn't want to switch to a different model. 4. I bought the same model again with the intention of just using it if the problem occurred again. 5. Looking at dishwasher reviews, Samsung products are said to be the best (I previously replaced my SK 3-place setting model because it was too small). I am hoping that this issue won't happen this time.

Comments (English): [ The installers are always friendly ] || ---------------- || It arrived and was installed in just two days. I don't usually write reviews, but I felt I had to this time. This is also the reason I deducted one star. I had the same model Samsung dishwasher installed in October 2023 and used it well for nearly three months. However, starting around the end of December, detergent powder started appearing on the dishes and inside the dishwasher (I have attached a photo below), so I requested an after-sales service. The technician came, inspected it, and confirmed it was detergent powder. He told me to reduce the amount of detergent used (as shown in the photo, half the original amount was being used). When I said I was using less, he told me to use rinse aid instead. I was already using rinse aid. He suggested I try changing the detergent, specifically liquid detergent instead of solid detergent. However, the problem persists even after switching. The same issue occurred with the SK 3-place setting detergent I used before switching to solid detergent. Doesn't that imply a problem with the dishwasher? He claims there is nothing wrong because the dishwasher is working properly. He told me to call him if the issue persists even after changing the detergent and running it on the "Powerful" setting. I called the technician and sent him photos saying the problem was exactly the same. He then told me to send a video showing the white substance forming inside the dishwasher and to get a water quality check. I don't understand. If he had said that from the beginning, I would have assumed it was a problem with the minerals or the composition of the tap water, as he claimed. However, it used to clean perfectly well before. I asked the apartment complex, and they said they haven't had any water inspections or replacements since September. Despite this, the technician claimed that the phenomenon is caused by the temperature difference between the tap water and detergent components, and told me to use something like a water purifier filter at the water outlet if it bothered me too much. When I asked if he was crazy and why I would use the dishwasher like that, he insisted it wasn't defective and tried to teach me about water purification. Furious, I called another technician. He said the same thing. In the end, I told him to take the dishwasher away because I couldn't use it. The second technician said he would have the customer service center report how the previous technician acted and would look into a refund without further ado, but he left with the possibility that it might not work out. He said he would pass on the message to the company's top manager demanding a refund, and if that worked, he would issue it. The next day, I received a call asking me to send a photo of the receipt. I attached five photos and sent a picture of the receipt, and they said they would issue a refund, so I received it. The reasons I purchased the same model again are: 1. The price is reasonable. 2. It was convenient to use as the cutlery holder is located at the front. 3. Since I had been using it, I was used to it and didn't want to switch to a different model. 4. I bought the same model again with the intention of just using it if the problem occurred again. 5. Looking at dishwasher reviews, Samsung products are said to be the best (I previously replaced my SK 3-place setting model because it was too small). I am hoping that this issue won't happen this time.

Comments (English): [ The installers are always friendly ] || ---------------- || It arrived and was installed in just two days. I don't usually write reviews, but I felt I had to this time. This is also the reason I deducted one star. I had the same model Samsung dishwasher installed in October 2023 and used it well for nearly three months. However, starting around the end of December, detergent powder started appearing on the dishes and inside the dishwasher (I have attached a photo below), so I requested an after-sales service. The technician came, inspected it, and confirmed it was detergent powder. He told me to reduce the amount of detergent used (as shown in the photo, half the original amount was being used). When I said I was using less, he told me to use rinse aid instead. I was already using rinse aid. He suggested I try changing the detergent, specifically liquid detergent instead of solid detergent. However, the problem persists even after switching. The same issue occurred with the SK 3-place setting detergent I used before switching to solid detergent. Doesn't that imply a problem with the dishwasher? He claims there is nothing wrong because the dishwasher is working properly. He told me to call him if the issue persists even after changing the detergent and running it on the "Powerful" setting. I called the technician and sent him photos saying the problem was exactly the same. He then told me to send a video showing the white substance forming inside the dishwasher and to get a water quality check. I don't understand. If he had said that from the beginning, I would have assumed it was a problem with the minerals or the composition of the tap water, as he claimed. However, it used to clean perfectly well before. I asked the apartment complex, and they said they haven't had any water inspections or replacements since September. Despite this, the technician claimed that the phenomenon is caused by the temperature difference between the tap water and detergent components, and told me to use something like a water purifier filter at the water outlet if it bothered me too much. When I asked if he was crazy and why I would use the dishwasher like that, he insisted it wasn't defective and tried to teach me about water purification. Furious, I called another technician. He said the same thing. In the end, I told him to take the dishwasher away because I couldn't use it. The second technician said he would have the customer service center report how the previous technician acted and would look into a refund without further ado, but he left with the possibility that it might not work out. He said he would pass on the message to the company's top manager demanding a refund, and if that worked, he would issue it. The next day, I received a call asking me to send a photo of the receipt. I attached five photos and sent a picture of the receipt, and they said they would issue a refund, so I received it. The reasons I purchased the same model again are: 1. The price is reasonable. 2. It was convenient to use as the cutlery holder is located at the front. 3. Since I had been using it, I was used to it and didn't want to switch to a different model. 4. I bought the same model again with the intention of just using it if the problem occurred again. 5. Looking at dishwasher reviews, Samsung products are said to be the best (I previously replaced my SK 3-place setting model because it was too small). I am hoping that this issue won't happen this time.

Comments (English): [ The installers are always friendly ] || ---------------- || It arrived and was installed in just two days. I don't usually write reviews, but I felt I had to this time. This is also the reason I deducted one star. I had the same model Samsung dishwasher installed in October 2023 and used it well for nearly three months. However, starting around the end of December, detergent powder started appearing on the dishes and inside the dishwasher (I have attached a photo below), so I requested an after-sales service. The technician came, inspected it, and confirmed it was detergent powder. He told me to reduce the amount of detergent used (as shown in the photo, half the original amount was being used). When I said I was using less, he told me to use rinse aid instead. I was already using rinse aid. He suggested I try changing the detergent, specifically liquid detergent instead of solid detergent. However, the problem persists even after switching. The same issue occurred with the SK 3-place setting detergent I used before switching to solid detergent. Doesn't that imply a problem with the dishwasher? He claims there is nothing wrong because the dishwasher is working properly. He told me to call him if the issue persists even after changing the detergent and running it on the "Powerful" setting. I called the technician and sent him photos saying the problem was exactly the same. He then told me to send a video showing the white substance forming inside the dishwasher and to get a water quality check. I don't understand. If he had said that from the beginning, I would have assumed it was a problem with the minerals or the composition of the tap water, as he claimed. However, it used to clean perfectly well before. I asked the apartment complex, and they said they haven't had any water inspections or replacements since September. Despite this, the technician claimed that the phenomenon is caused by the temperature difference between the tap water and detergent components, and told me to use something like a water purifier filter at the water outlet if it bothered me too much. When I asked if he was crazy and why I would use the dishwasher like that, he insisted it wasn't defective and tried to teach me about water purification. Furious, I called another technician. He said the same thing. In the end, I told him to take the dishwasher away because I couldn't use it. The second technician said he would have the customer service center report how the previous technician acted and would look into a refund without further ado, but he left with the possibility that it might not work out. He said he would pass on the message to the company's top manager demanding a refund, and if that worked, he would issue it. The next day, I received a call asking me to send a photo of the receipt. I attached five photos and sent a picture of the receipt, and they said they would issue a refund, so I received it. The reasons I purchased the same model again are: 1. The price is reasonable. 2. It was convenient to use as the cutlery holder is located at the front. 3. Since I had been using it, I was used to it and didn't want to switch to a different model. 4. I bought the same model again with the intention of just using it if the problem occurred again. 5. Looking at dishwasher reviews, Samsung products are said to be the best (I previously replaced my SK 3-place setting model because it was too small). I am hoping that this issue won't happen this time.

Comments (English): [ The installers are always friendly ] || ---------------- || It arrived and was installed in just two days. I don't usually write reviews, but I felt I had to this time. This is also the reason I deducted one star. I had the same model Samsung dishwasher installed in October 2023 and used it well for nearly three months. However, starting around the end of December, detergent powder started appearing on the dishes and inside the dishwasher (I have attached a photo below), so I requested an after-sales service. The technician came, inspected it, and confirmed it was detergent powder. He told me to reduce the amount of detergent used (as shown in the photo, half the original amount was being used). When I said I was using less, he told me to use rinse aid instead. I was already using rinse aid. He suggested I try changing the detergent, specifically liquid detergent instead of solid detergent. However, the problem persists even after switching. The same issue occurred with the SK 3-place setting detergent I used before switching to solid detergent. Doesn't that imply a problem with the dishwasher? He claims there is nothing wrong because the dishwasher is working properly. He told me to call him if the issue persists even after changing the detergent and running it on the "Powerful" setting. I called the technician and sent him photos saying the problem was exactly the same. He then told me to send a video showing the white substance forming inside the dishwasher and to get a water quality check. I don't understand. If he had said that from the beginning, I would have assumed it was a problem with the minerals or the composition of the tap water, as he claimed. However, it used to clean perfectly well before. I asked the apartment complex, and they said they haven't had any water inspections or replacements since September. Despite this, the technician claimed that the phenomenon is caused by the temperature difference between the tap water and detergent components, and told me to use something like a water purifier filter at the water outlet if it bothered me too much. When I asked if he was crazy and why I would use the dishwasher like that, he insisted it wasn't defective and tried to teach me about water purification. Furious, I called another technician. He said the same thing. In the end, I told him to take the dishwasher away because I couldn't use it. The second technician said he would have the customer service center report how the previous technician acted and would look into a refund without further ado, but he left with the possibility that it might not work out. He said he would pass on the message to the company's top manager demanding a refund, and if that worked, he would issue it. The next day, I received a call asking me to send a photo of the receipt. I attached five photos and sent a picture of the receipt, and they said they would issue a refund, so I received it. The reasons I purchased the same model again are: 1. The price is reasonable. 2. It was convenient to use as the cutlery holder is located at the front. 3. Since I had been using it, I was used to it and didn't want to switch to a different model. 4. I bought the same model again with the intention of just using it if the problem occurred again. 5. Looking at dishwasher reviews, Samsung products are said to be the best (I previously replaced my SK 3-place setting model because it was too small). I am hoping that this issue won't happen this time.

This basically means that we have to run the dishwasher once a day on weekdays, but commonly twice a day on the weekends. The complaint I have is the spacing of the tines, and the placement really makes it hard to efficiently fill the dishwasher. Because of the spacing of the tines, pans will not stand up in the dishwasher and fall over, laying almost flat on the bottom of any of the racks, effectively stealing space for other dishes. slightly taller tines with fewer tines could remedy this and make the dishwasher more efficient to fill. Otherwise, all the other features seem well-designed, once you order the accessory set. It really is a shame that this didn't come with the accessory set. It should have. I just bought it, and it seems like a practical thing to have, and a better-designed silverware basket that should have been the factory-provided silverware basket. The adjustable and removable top rack is awesome. Comments (English): [ Unfriendly user interface ] || ---------------- || Many things I dislike. The door slams shut such that it would be easy to jam and bruise your hand. The Home Connect (wi-fi) app is confusing. Inconveniently, delay start can only be set from a phone via Home Connect, not on the dishwasher itself, and it took me a long time to figure out how to enable it. The notches in the upper shelf holder for stemmed glassware are too narrow to hold my ordinary size wine glasses. It takes a few pushes to firmly close the soap dispenser; the latch is pretty weak. The control panel doesn't have clearly defined buttons to press, just flat text beneath a small light, so it generally takes a few taps to find the right spot to elicit a response. Further, the labels/text on the "buttons" shown in the user manual don't match those on the actual dishwasher. The dishwasher is very quiet and washes dishes well, but for this user there are too many annoyances in operating it.

I'll have to say that this unit probably isn't the most efficient or innovative (except for the Crystal Dry). However, it works well and has that "knock on wood" quality.

I wish the bottom racks had adjustable space width where you can fold up/down the tongs to create thinner/wider spaces to fit thinner/thicker plates/pans as needed. Sentence (English): I choose the Bosch after looking at multiple youtube reviews, especially those made by actual repair technicians.
Comments (English): [ Built to last ] || ---------------- || I choose the Bosch after looking at multiple youtube reviews, especially those made by actual repair technicians. Overwhelmingly, the technician surveys prefer Bosch to other major brands based on their repair experience. My previous dishwasher, a KitchenAid wasn't a low end model, but required a new circulator pump after six years, and a drain pump after 7. The interior also had a lot of plastic, which became brittle over time and required periodic replacement of certain parts.The Bosch has far less plastic. It doesn't use a heating element, which also I believe contributed to previous dishwasher making plastic brittle.Finally, I wanted to move over to a system that had a easily cleaned filter. The Kitchenaid I used had a grinder pump. While it worked for a long time, at the end it was recirulating debris, and I was not able to access the grinder blade compartment. I'd much rather clean out an easy to pull out filter every few weeks knowing that it is filtering the smallest particles out that would eventually have caused problems later.The only thing I liked about the kitchen aid was the LED screen showing progress. The Bosch is simpler, with just a red light showing it's in progress. To get actually remaining time I neeed to use the App. Not a big deal, it's pretty much 2 hours a lot, give or take some.

Sentence (English): I installed this dish washer 2 weeks ago and the jury is still out on it.
Comments (English): [ Poor design and performance ] || ---------------- || I installed this dish washer 2 weeks ago and the jury is still out on it. First of all, it's the noisiest dishwasher I've owned. It's advertised as whisper quiet and during the washing cycle you can hear the water swishing loudly around for approximately 1/2 hour. Was told it's my water pressure and it's not the water pressure, it's the machine. We had a new water pressure gauge installed just last summer and we have great, consistent water pressure. The 2 nd shelf lifts up and/ or down or tilts either high on low right and left side, so I thought great, I can tilt the 2nd shelf high on one side to accommodate cookie sheets and it drops down on the other side to allow a large glass, but when you do that, the dishwasher door doesn't close as now the 2nd shelf doesn't align with the fittings in the rear of the dishwasher. So you must either lift the shelf evenly , either up or down. Tall glasses are an issue on the 2 nd shelf due to the 3rd shelf interfering and if you need the 2nd shelf up high to accommodate large items in the bottom shelf, it just doesn't work……a long explanation, but it's a problem. Had to remove the cutlery handle as it interferes with allowing you to put cutlery in the holder anywhere near the handle area….blocks usage. Unless you have the machine set to high dry boost, don't expect your dishes to come out 100% dry, especially plastics. Had a flat bottomed stainless pot on the bottom shelf ( inverted) and when I took it out of the dishwasher after the cycle, the top of the bottom was very wet and spilled on my hardwood floors. Had a very small cup on the 3rd shelf which had a bit of ketchup in it and after washing completed, the ketchup was still in the cup….didn't come clean. There is only 2 of us so not many dishes so machine is never overloaded. I will adjust to its deficiencies, but I don't know if I can live with the noise this washer creates, especially after reading the description that it is super quiet! Extremely disappointed in this dishwasher. Maybe I just got a lemon. Positive? It looks great and matches my LG fridge

Sentence (English): I've had this dishwasher since 2018, used when i got it.
Comments (English): [ Easy to repair. ] || ---------------- || I've had this dishwasher since 2018, used when i got it. It's been great as of 2024.I've replaced the main computer board $50, top rack screws $10, and the short little rubber elbow hose that's on the drain pump, 4$ for sealant and a random piece of hose i had. This dishwasher has cost $64 to maintain over 6 years. Each repair has taken 15 minutes at the max, easy as heck. Yes, i source my parts on ebay for good prices, but all the parts are new! I see a few reviews about the controls glitching out. I paid 50 dollars for that control board and it's fixed. Yes, that requires you to grab a screw driver and use it. This dishwasher is built in such a way, repair's are crazy easy. I think ill get another 5 years out of this machine with simple repair's. My drain pump repair was a little more hands on as i wanted to reuse the pump, But they sell whole drain pump kits. Plug and play with 2 hoseclamps! Stop writing a bad review on a appliance you've had for 4+ years and just fix it yourself. I will say, don't forget to make sure that fill hose is in after a repair. That does suck. Worried about leaks going unnoticed? they sell leak alarms/detectors on amazon, and appliance drain pans you sit your appliance in. After buying all that, plus the parts, you'd still need another $500 to buy a new stainless machine.

Sentence (English): I choose the Bosch after looking at multiple youtube reviews, especially those made by actual repair technicians.
Comments (English): [ Built to last ] || ---------------- || I choose the Bosch after looking at multiple youtube reviews, especially those made by actual repair technicians. Overwhelmingly, the technician surveys prefer Bosch to other major brands based on their repair experience. My previous dishwasher, a KitchenAid wasn't a low end model, but required a new circulator pump after six years, and a drain pump after 7. The interior also had a lot of plastic, which became brittle over time and required periodic replacement of certain parts. The Bosch has far less plastic. It doesn't use a heating element, which also I believe contributed to previous dishwasher making plastic brittle. Finally, I wanted to move over to a system that had a easily cleaned filter. The Kitchenaid I used had a grinder pump. While it worked for a long time, at the end it was recirulating debris, and I was not able to access the grinder blade compartment. I'd much rather clean out an easy to pull out filter every few weeks knowing that it is filtering the smallest particles out that would eventually have caused problems later. The only thing I liked about the kitchen aid was the LED screen showing progress. The Bosch is simpler, with just a red light showing it's in progress. To get actually remaining time I neeed to use the App. Not a big deal, it's pretty much 2 hours a lot, give or take some.

The interior also had a lot of plastic, which became brittle over time and required periodic replacement of certain parts. The Bosch has far less plastic. It doesn't use a heating element, which also I believe contributed to previous dishwasher making plastic brittle. Finally, I wanted to move over to a system that had a easily cleaned filter. The Kitchenaid I used had a grinder pump. While it worked for a long time, at the end it was recirulating debris, and I was not able to access the grinder blade compartment. I'd much rather clean out an easy to pull out filter every few weeks knowing that it is filtering the smallest particles out that would eventually have caused problems later. The only thing I liked about the kitchen aid was the LED screen showing progress. The Bosch is simpler, with just a red light showing it's in progress. To get actually remaining time I neeed to use the App. Not a big deal, it's pretty much 2 hours a lot, give or take some.

Sentence (English): I bought this dishwasher on the 2023 Thanksgiving/December sale.
Comments (English): [ Impressive ] || ---------------- || I bought this dishwasher on the 2023 Thanksgiving/December sale. It replaced a GE dishwasher I bought from Costco in 2017. I really liked that dishwasher - super quiet, fast cycle (80 minutes. though more like 90), and just nice overall. But the electronics were never right. I had GE Appliances out twice and they replaced the control panel and motherboard. yet it still malfunctioned at 6 years. If you didn't use it every day in the final few months it just turned itself off and was super hard to start (literally unplug, replug in, a few times). Okay, so let me introduce "Colossus", as I have named it. It's huge. It is a little big in the spot (sticks out more), but the 3rd rack is actually super useful. My GE had 2 rotating arms and a sprayer at the top. This bad boy has three rotating arms (top one is small, but rotates! ), and the water spray system for the 3rd rack, for a total of 4 washing systems. Okay, so it is 47DB, but has a distinctive swish swish pause swooch sound. I'm pretty sure it is the 3rd rack that drives the sound. It's pretty quiet, and doesn't really disturb my TV watching in the adjacent Great Room. Okay, so what's so great? The 3rd rack is actually useful. I don't put bowls on it like they advertise (too short but for small bowls). I put the plastic reusable containers on there, along with my coffee cups. I also wash my scissors, hand scrubber, tongs, sponges, measuring cups, and any miscellaneous small stuff up there. It's actually very useful. The stainless steel tub is lovely, but not perfect. not sure on the control processes, but there are a few 'dents'. It doesn't impact the usefulness of the washer. So, why did I rate 5 stars instead of 4? Well, I'd buy it again. It's huge. Reasonably quiet. The dishes are clean. I saw complaints that it takes too long to wash a load. Well, you can do a 'quick wash' in an hour I think, but I just do normal in 2 hours and 30 minutes. I don't need the heated dry. It's fine. I just care that they are nice and clean. I hope it lasts 10 years unlike my former GE dishwasher. But it's got the right things - cleans dishes well, is reasonably quiet, and is really enormous. If you have 4+ people in your family, I think you would benefit from this or it's cousins branded as Maytag or Kitchen Aid. They're all the same machine, just with various differences.

Comments (English): [ Installation Nightmare ] || ---------------- || This is a review for the service only. Dishwasher is pretty good. I don't have any problem with it and I would rate it as 5 start. But the installation service is a nightmare. I had to pay $179 for dishwasher installation, but the whole process has been a complete disaster. BestBuy seems to be using two different contractors for this service, which has resulted in a month-long wait filled with lack of communication, confusion, and uselessness. I am extremely frustrated and I believe I deserve reimbursement for this ordeal. Day one: The first guy came to deliver my dishwasher, but during the installation, he claimed that the hose was broken ( or he broke it? ). I'm waiting for the new hose to be delivered and replaced. When the hose was delivered, another individual showed up to install it. Unfortunately, while installing the hose, he accidentally messed up with the disposal, causing it to stop working. I had to contact him and ask him to come back and fix the problem, which he did eventually. Day three: A couple of days later, the garbage disposal stopped working again. I reached out to the service once more and requested them to come and fix the problem. A couple of (new! ) guys came over and shockingly started removing the dishwasher. I was perplexed and questioned them about their actions. They said they came to replace the dishwasher, which I found absurd. I clarified that they needed to fix my disposal instead. Thankfully, they managed to fix it and explained the issue to me. Even after enduring all these troubles, my dishwasher is still poorly attached to the counter top, and the power switch is loose. Additionally, every time these companies call me, they inquire about dishwasher installation, despite the fact that it has already been installed. I repeatedly have to explain that I just need other related problem to be fixed. This whole installation experience has been incredibly frustrating and I'm disappointed in the lack of professionalism and efficiency from BestBuy and its contractors. I strongly request reimbursement for this entire ordeal.

Sentence (English): Bosch dishwashers have a great reputation for a reason: they're great.
Comments (English): [ Quiet and excellent, mostly ] || ---------------- || Bosch dishwashers have a great reputation for a reason: they're great. Quieter than anything else out there, great wash quality, and better than average rack designs and quality. Overall we've had no issues with the machine over several years, and I'd buy one again. I would give this a full 5 stars, except for a couple design flaws. One minor one is that the counter fastening system is mediocre, makes it hard to really secure the machine where it won't shift at all. More importantly, though manageable, is that it will spray water on your floor if you put a hemispherical bowl in a front corner of the lower rack. You may think it's a bad seal and replace it, but it's not, it's quite simply engineered that way - if water incidentally sprays towards a forward corner, it will come out. This is manageable by just putting your hemispherical bowls anywhere else, but annoying because it's the best place to put one.

It would help if somebody added a how to load a dishwasher properly as many people aren't sure where to put bowls or whether to put things right side up or upside down.

Sentence (English): We bought our Bosch 800 series dishwasher in 12-2023 after reading a lot of glowing reviews of various Bosch dishwasher models.
Comments (English): [ Bosch is King of Dishwashers ] || ---------------- || We bought our Bosch 800 series dishwasher in 12-2023 after reading a lot of glowing reviews of various Bosch dishwasher models. We were most concerned with reliability, quietness and good capacity for dishes. After about 1 month, we can say that the Bosch is very quiet and has a large capacity for dishes. Everything seems to be working fine.We do not run the dishwasher more that 1-2 times per week (2 person household) so we have multiple meals worth of silverware and therefore decided to buy a second silverware basket to supplement the one that came with the machine. This works out great. While the 3rd upper rack can hold silverware, we like the basket to carry it over to our silverware drawer.One suggestion we have is to include a few pages of basic operating instructions with the machine when it is installed. It was confusing to us as to how & when to change the wash cycle and select the drying cycle. Also it was not clear whether Crystal Dry cycle was suppose to work with all wash cycles. Since we got many page about installation and warranty info, why not a little info about basic operations. We called the Bosch 800 phone number and got all our questions answered, including about wifi and bluetooth, and would say that the Bosch Phone Rep was excellent and our wait time was minimal. Good work! All is all, we are very happy with our Bosch dishwasher at this point.

Sentence (English): This is a review for the service only.
Comments (English): [ Installation Nightmare ] || ---------------- || This is a review for the service only. Dishwasher is pretty good. I don't have any problem with it and I would rate it as 5 start. But the installation service is a nightmare.I had to pay $179 for dishwasher installation, but the whole process has been a complete disaster. BestBuy seems to be using two different contractors for this service, which has resulted in a month-long wait filled with lack of communication, confusion, and uselessness. I am extremely frustrated and I believe I deserve reimbursement for this ordeal.Day one: The first guy came to deliver my dishwasher, but during the installation, he claimed that the hose was broken ( or he broke it? ). Despite this issue, he managed to do a great job with the installation.Since it was a pretty much same model, he replaced the broken hose with an old one, ensuring everything worked properly. This was crucial since it happened just a couple of days before Christmas.However, the hose still needs to be replaced, as it should be covered by warranty. I'm waiting for the new hose to be delivered and replaced.Day two: Another person, possibly from a different company (I'm not even sure anymore, and it's frustrating that I have to keep track of all these different people and companies when I've already paid for the service), called me asking for my address to deliver the hose. When the hose was delivered, another individual showed up to install it. Unfortunately, while installing the hose, he accidentally messed up with the disposal, causing it to stop working. I had to contact him and ask him to come back and fix the problem, which he did eventually.Day three: A couple of days later, the garbage disposal stopped working again. I reached out to the service once more and requested them to come and fix the problem. A couple of (new! ) guys came over and shockingly started removing the dishwasher. I was perplexed and questioned them about their actions. They said they came to replace the dishwasher, which I found absurd. I clarified that they needed to fix my disposal instead. Thankfully, they managed to fix it and explained the issue to me.Even after enduring all these troubles, my dishwasher is still poorly attached to the counter top, and the power switch is loose. Additionally, every time these companies call me, they inquire about dishwasher installation, despite the fact that it has already been installed. I repeatedly have to explain that I just need other related problem to be fixed.This whole installation experience has been incredibly frustrating and I'm disappointed in the lack of professionalism and efficiency from BestBuy and its contractors. I strongly request reimbursement for this entire ordeal.

Sentence (English): I bought this dishwasher about three years ago from Costco over in Peachtree city Georgia.
Comments (English): [ doesn't last long. ] || ---------------- || I bought this dishwasher about three years ago from Costco over in Peachtree city Georgia. I bought it as part of a set for a four piece kitchen package, as well as a four piece washer and dryer package. Costco came out delivered and installed it. I am single and live alone, and I use the washer maybe once or twice a month. After about two years and two months, the Touch panel on the top of the door started to malfunction. Then it completely went out. I called Costco to see if there was something that they could do. Of course, I was outside of the two-year warranty by a few weeks, and they were unable to do anything. I reached out to a local repair guy that I had in the past and he informed me that this product has had known problems. So he reached out to LG and found out that they would extend the warranty for the touch panel, but not the power source. The total to repair including installation would be $400. It's a nice dishwasher and very quiet. If you have counters that extend out, you will have to turn the machine on and then you have like five seconds to close it and then it will automatically start. I'm thinking in the future. I will look at one where the buttons are on the front. so I'm torn between spending $800 on a brand new one or going to a cheaper version for 550 or paying $400 to repair the one that's brand new barely been used. I would definitely recommend buying the extended warranty. You get two years with Costco but if you use your credit card with Costco Citi card, I believe they extended up to five years. It would be nice if you were able to use your American Express platinum because you would get five years extended warranty with the $50 deductible.

Sentence (English): The area around the vent and at the bottom of the door is rusting.
Comments (English): [ Rust On Door ] || ---------------- || The area around the vent and at the bottom of the door is rusting. It looks like the finish (perhaps the clear coat they put on to mitigate fingerprints) doesn't seal correctly near the edges and so the rust begins to grow between the stainless steel as the clear finish. After attempting to clean it with safe appliance cleaners I realized the rust was underneath the clear coat (I could see the clear coat was lifting from the stainless steel) so after removing the flaking coating I was able to remove most of the rust but there are still some rust stains (pictures are AFTER cleaning the peeling coat debris and removing the rust that I could). But now the finish is uneven (though it's better than the circle of rush around the vent I guess). I bought this dishwasher because I loved the design of the third rack. I also had bought a Kitchen Aid oven the year prior that matched and was really thought I was investing in a quality brand. I've looked online to see if I can put a new door on it but I can't seem to find the right one for this model. I'm just so disappointed as it looks so dirty and beat up and it's under two years old.

Sentence (English): The thing I hate most about housework is washing dishes, so I've entered the new world of dishwashers.
Comments (English): [ I regret it. ] || ---------------- || The thing I hate most about housework is washing dishes, so I've entered the new world of dishwashers. The water tank is at the bottom, so it doesn't seem that noisy. I think sound-absorbing material or something would work. The most disappointing thing is that the trays are not very tight. Even without that, I can only fit a few items, and they keep falling through the gaps. (I bought a 1,000 won net from Daitaeo, so it fits roughly.) Leaving everything else aside, I chose this product for an extra 100,000 won because of the door opening function, but I only use it when I'm at home, so it seems like a function I don't need (When I'm done, I can put a clothespin or a small doll between the doors if I'm worried about scratches). Additional 1. I wonder if I'm putting the detergent in wrong, but it would be nice if there was a rinse function when there's a stain. This made me think about it.
