It does come off, but it's difficult and a hassle. Although it's a hassle, I filled the container they sent me with water three times and used it. It spilled between the container and the dishwasher, so I think I'll have to try the dishwasher. The water inlet is wide, but I think it would have been better if it was a little taller. Addition 2. You mentioned the rinse function, and when I ran it quickly once more, it didn't show any stains and felt clean. Addition 3. Rather than putting water in the container they sent, it's faster to refill it with a wide water container I bought at Da-it-o without spilling (photo attached). Addition 4. To prevent it from continuing to run in the dryer when I go out after using it, I installed a remote timer? (Photo attached). It seems good because you can schedule the off time and turn it off remotely.

Comments (English): [ The color is a bit disappointing. ] || ---------------- || Our sink is on the far left wall, so I installed it there. Since it's only 600 sheets, I thought I could just put it in after removing the bottom, but when I checked with LG customer service, they said that the freestanding model has the front legs right in front, so there are no bolts on either side, but the built-in model has the front legs a bit back because of the mop holder, so it's unstable, so they said that you have to put in a bolt on each side right when you open the door to install it. (In the picture of the open door, you can see a bolt cap on the top center of each side of the sink. That's the fixed bolt.) So you need a piece of wood that can be attached to either side or fixed. However, the wall side of my house has a finishing film for the lower cabinet of the sink, but it's connected to the removed 600 sheet and is only fixed to the wall with silicone, so it's dangling. And since it's at the end, I removed the 600 sheet that was supporting the top, so I had to do some work on the top. The installer called to schedule an installation time on a weekday, but he said it had to be done before 6 PM, so I postponed it to Saturday and asked about the additional cost. They said an additional 80,000 won would be added to the cost of installing the support and bolting the side wall together with the Fila. It seemed simple enough, so I decided to try it myself. I scavenged some lumber from the junkyard and inserted one piece each on the front and back of the left wall for support. Since the wall was made of drywall, I just installed the pieces and applied some silicone where it felt loose. For the Fila, I roughly picked up three pieces of Daruki that overlapped each other, making sure they were the right size. Since the wall was made of marble, it might break if I drove it in, so I just applied silicone glue and stuck it on. I let it dry, letting it collect on the bottom and sides for a day. The next day, I used pieces to attach the Fila to the wood I'd glued with silicone. But it was too much work. I think it's better to just pay the 80,000 won. If the dishwasher door were the same size as the lower cabinet door, the SLA would fit perfectly, but that's not the case, so I installed it to match the SLA below. My wife chose the dubj4el model, and it comes in three colors: beige, dark teal?, and a later cream. Since none of the colors matched our cabinets, I just went with the plain beige, but I don't like it. It looks cheaper than the sink door. Samsung seems to have a more beveled steel version, which is a bit disappointing. I think I'll be able to use it for 10 years. I installed it yesterday and used it once, and when I tested tap water with a water hardness test kit, it was hard water level 1. Level 0 is soft water and doesn't need salt, and level 1 is water that can be used for 10 weeks with 1 kilogram of refined salt. The higher the hardness, the more salt is used. The installer said that not many households use salt except in rural areas. I ran the standard test and it said it would take about 2 hours, but after about an hour, the door opened and it seemed to be drying. I wonder why it takes so long to wash dishes. Reviews are full of praise, saying it's a new world and why I only bought it now, but I still don't get it.

Comments (English): [ The color is a bit disappointing. ] || ---------------- || Our sink is on the far left wall, so I installed it there. Since it's only 600 sheets, I thought I could just put it in after removing the bottom, but when I checked with LG customer service, they said that the freestanding model has the front legs right in front, so there are no bolts on either side, but the built-in model has the front legs a bit back because of the mop holder, so it's unstable, so they said that you have to put in a bolt on each side right when you open the door to install it. (In the picture of the open door, you can see a bolt cap on the top center of each side of the sink. That's the fixed bolt.) So you need a piece of wood that can be attached to either side or fixed. However, the wall side of my house has a finishing film for the lower cabinet of the sink, but it's connected to the removed 600 sheet and is only fixed to the wall with silicone, so it's dangling. And since it's at the end, I removed the 600 sheet that was supporting the top, so I had to do some work on the top. The installer called to schedule an installation time on a weekday, but he said it had to be done before 6 PM, so I postponed it to Saturday and asked about the additional cost. They said an additional 80,000 won would be added to the cost of installing the support and bolting the side wall together with the Fila. It seemed simple enough, so I decided to try it myself. I scavenged some lumber from the junkyard and inserted one piece each on the front and back of the left wall for support. Since the wall was made of drywall, I just installed the pieces and applied some silicone where it felt loose. For the Fila, I roughly picked up three pieces of Daruki that overlapped each other, making sure they were the right size. Since the wall was made of marble, it might break if I drove it in, so I just applied silicone glue and stuck it on. I let it dry, letting it collect on the bottom and sides for a day. The next day, I used pieces to attach the Fila to the wood I'd glued with silicone. But it was too much work. I think it's better to just pay the 80,000 won. If the dishwasher door were the same size as the lower cabinet door, the SLA would fit perfectly, but that's not the case, so I installed it to match the SLA below. My wife chose the dubj4el model, and it comes in three colors: beige, dark teal?, and a later cream. Since none of the colors matched our cabinets, I just went with the plain beige, but I don't like it. It looks cheaper than the sink door. Samsung seems to have a more beveled steel version, which is a bit disappointing. I think I'll be able to use it for 10 years. I installed it yesterday and used it once, and when I tested tap water with a water hardness test kit, it was hard water level 1. Level 0 is soft water and doesn't need salt, and level 1 is water that can be used for 10 weeks with 1 kilogram of refined salt. The higher the hardness, the more salt is used. The installer said that not many households use salt except in rural areas. I ran the standard test and it said it would take about 2 hours, but after about an hour, the door opened and it seemed to be drying. I wonder why it takes so long to wash dishes. Reviews are full of praise, saying it's a new world and why I only bought it now, but I still don't get it.

The installer called to schedule an installation time on a weekday, but he said it had to be done before 6 PM, so I postponed it to Saturday and asked about the additional cost. They said an additional 80,000 won would be added to the cost of installing the support and bolting the side wall together with the Fila. It seemed simple enough, so I decided to try it myself. I scavenged some lumber from the junkyard and inserted one piece each on the front and back of the left wall for support. Since the wall was made of drywall, I just installed the pieces and applied some silicone where it felt loose. For the Fila, I roughly picked up three pieces of Daruki that overlapped each other, making sure they were the right size. The installer said that not many households use salt except in rural areas. I ran the standard test and it said it would take about 2 hours, but after about an hour, the door opened and it seemed to be drying. I wonder why it takes so long to wash dishes. Reviews are full of praise, saying it's a new world and why I only bought it now, but I still don't get it.

Comments (English): [ The color is a bit disappointing. ] || ---------------- || Our sink is on the far left wall, so I installed it there. (In the picture of the open door, you can see a bolt cap on the top center of each side of the sink. That's the fixed bolt.) So you need a piece of wood that can be attached to either side or fixed. However, the wall side of my house has a finishing film for the lower cabinet of the sink, but it's connected to the removed 600 sheet and is only fixed to the wall with silicone, so it's dangling. And since it's at the end, I removed the 600 sheet that was supporting the top, so I had to do some work on the top. The installer called to schedule an installation time on a weekday, but he said it had to be done before 6 PM, so I postponed it to Saturday and asked about the additional cost. They said an additional 80,000 won would be added to the cost of installing the support and bolting the side wall together with the Fila. It seemed simple enough, so I decided to try it myself. I scavenged some lumber from the junkyard and inserted one piece each on the front and back of the left wall for support. Since the wall was made of drywall, I just installed the pieces and applied some silicone where it felt loose. For the Fila, I roughly picked up three pieces of Daruki that overlapped each other, making sure they were the right size. Since the wall was made of marble, it might break if I drove it in, so I just applied silicone glue and stuck it on. I let it dry, letting it collect on the bottom and sides for a day. The next day, I used pieces to attach the Fila to the wood I'd glued with silicone. But it was too much work. I think it's better to just pay the 80,000 won. If the dishwasher door were the same size as the lower cabinet door, the SLA would fit perfectly, but that's not the case, so I installed it to match the SLA below. My wife chose the dubj4el model, and it comes in three colors: beige, dark teal?, and a later cream. Since none of the colors matched our cabinets, I just went with the plain beige, but I don't like it. It looks cheaper than the sink door. Samsung seems to have a more beveled steel version, which is a bit disappointing. I think I'll be able to use it for 10 years. I installed it yesterday and used it once, and when I tested tap water with a water hardness test kit, it was hard water level 1. Level 0 is soft water and doesn't need salt, and level 1 is water that can be used for 10 weeks with 1 kilogram of refined salt. The higher the hardness, the more salt is used. The installer said that not many households use salt except in rural areas. I ran the standard test and it said it would take about 2 hours, but after about an hour, the door opened and it seemed to be drying. I wonder why it takes so long to wash dishes. Reviews are full of praise, saying it's a new world and why I only bought it now, but I still don't get it.

Sentence (English): Pros: This is probably the best dishwasher we've ever owned.
Comments (English): [ Great Dishwasher, but don't need the smarts! ] || ---------------- || Pros: This is probably the best dishwasher we've ever owned. I'm 75 and have gone through several. We've had it now for several months and have never had to rewash anything. The racks are built to hold just about any dish or cup and with the tine fold down features it can easily do the pots and pans. Cons: the control panel was hard to understand, it took me several sessions before it made sense. The wifi feature, for us, is essentially useless. We don't need to be by the app that the dishwasher is done, and like all the "dumb" dishwashers we've had before we know how to check the level of the rinse agent, clean the filter without again being notified. How did we manage without wifi before! Bottom line: it's a great dishwasher with a bunch of bells and whistles hung on just because the could. or maybe to try and justify the engineers jobs.

Sentence (English): After our last two dishwashers failed after just a few years, we decided to spend the extra money to get a Bosch in the hope that it will last longer.
Comments (English): [ Overall nice dishwasher ] || ---------------- || After our last two dishwashers failed after just a few years, we decided to spend the extra money to get a Bosch in the hope that it will last longer. So far, we are happy with it. It works well and we like the feature where it pops open at the end of the cycle to cool down and air dry. The things we don't like so much; the top silverware tray, as things up there don't seem to get as clean as they should. And the adjustable top rack is nice, but even on the higher setting, we can't fit our 12" dinner plates without putting them around the outside edge of the lower rack. More space in between would be better, and get rid of the top silverware rack. We've only had it about a month so can't comment on reliability just yet, so fingers crossed the extra money was worth it.

Not sure how long dishwashers should last now a days , due to the display errors that we been getting lately, we are in need of a new one. I don't have any really bad review of the product just wishing it would have lasted for 10 yrs rather than just 5 yrs . But there is one glaring problem: it has too many tines, too close together, and at funky angles. This setup, I assume, is perfect for a family that uses lots of large plates, but few mugs, bowls, pint-glasses, wine-glasses, etc. Not us. Oh, not just lots of tines but (on the lower rack) almost no horizontal bars either so big bowls don't really fit unless tipped over. The good news is that the upper rack can be lowered and while the tines there are weird, at least I have a place for big coffee mugs, etc. The attached picture is a random snapshot, but basically shows the problem. Upper shelf is packed. Lower shelf is empty because nothing else will fit. This means we now do 2 washes a day whereas we did one previously, which gets me to my next peeve: there is no way of knowing if the dishwasher has run. Most dishwashers have an LED or something to indicate completion whereas this dishwasher just goes silent to indicate completion. This is annoying mistake for an expensive dishwasher. Cleaning efficiency is average. Seems not uncommon to find a stained spoon or something. Note that I do not, in the slightest, wash anything before it goes into the machine, so maybe that is my fault. The good (almost bad! ) news is that the dishwasher is amazingly silent. So easy, in fact, for half the family to assume that it has never even been turned on. It has a light shining down to the floor when the dishwasher is active, but my kids seem to always ignore that and open the door anyway. Not really Bosch's fault! This gets me to completely irrelevant detail, but still somewhat irritating. If ever you find that you need to cancel a run, then the Bosch instructions say \"hold the Cancel button for 5 seconds\". There is no Cancel button. Only a \"Start/Resume\" button. but yes, holding the \"Start\" button is indeed how to cancel. Now we know. One other problem is likely my fault because I haven't called Best Buy to come and fix it yet, but \"Start\" doesn't work, at least not by itself. You have to hold the Reset button for 5 seconds and [only] then does the Start button work to initiate the dishwasher cycle. It also seems to get confused if ever the main power supply is turned off, so we always leave it powered on now. The combination of software/electrical issues and high price drops my rating from 5 stars to 4. But not being able to really load up the dishwasher gets me to a 3 - it puts me in a bad mood whenever I load the dishes.

But there is one glaring problem: it has too many tines, too close together, and at funky angles. This setup, I assume, is perfect for a family that uses lots of large plates, but few mugs, bowls, pint-glasses, wine-glasses, etc. Not us. Oh, not just lots of tines but (on the lower rack) almost no horizontal bars either so big bowls don't really fit unless tipped over. The good news is that the upper rack can be lowered and while the tines there are weird, at least I have a place for big coffee mugs, etc. The attached picture is a random snapshot, but basically shows the problem. Upper shelf is packed. Lower shelf is empty because nothing else will fit.This means we now do 2 washes a day whereas we did one previously, which gets me to my next peeve: there is no way of knowing if the dishwasher has run. Most dishwashers have an LED or something to indicate completion whereas this dishwasher just goes silent to indicate completion. This is annoying mistake for an expensive dishwasher. Cleaning efficiency is average. Seems not uncommon to find a stained spoon or something. Note that I do not, in the slightest, wash anything before it goes into the machine, so maybe that is my fault.The good (almost bad!) news is that the dishwasher is amazingly silent. So easy, in fact, for half the family to assume that it has never even been turned on. It has a light shining down to the floor when the dishwasher is active, but my kids seem to always ignore that and open the door anyway. Not really Bosch's fault!!!This gets me to completely irrelevant detail, but still somewhat irritating. If ever you find that you need to cancel a run, then the Bosch instructions say \'hold the Cancel button for 5 seconds\'. There is no Cancel button.  Only a \'Start/Resume\' button... but yes, holding the \'Start\' button is indeed how to cancel. Now we know.One other problem is likely my fault because I haven't called Best Buy to come and fix it yet, but \'Start\' doesn't work, at least not by itself. You have to hold the Reset button for 5 seconds and [only] then does the Start button work to initiate the dishwasher cycle. It also seems to get confused if ever the main power supply is turned off, so we always leave it powered on now.The combination of software/electrical issues and high price drops my rating from 5 stars to 4. Sentence (English): I thought the rebate offer online was very misleading.
Comments (English): [ Be Wary of Rebate Offers ] || ---------------- || I thought the rebate offer online was very misleading. Nowhere on the Lowes website did it specify that i had to purchase more than one appliance to be eligible for the rebate. The website just said 'Limit 1 per customer' with no mention of the fact that it was a Bosch rebate or any other details about the rebate. I assign partial blame to both Lowes and Bosch. I never would have purchased a $1000 dishwasher if I thought I wasn't eligible for the rebate. I even talked with a Lowes representative who assured me I was eligible. The rebate offer link on the Lowes website directed me to the Bosch rebate online claim form which just asked for a copy of the invoice, date of purchase, model # and serial #. I couldn't submit the form until after I had received the product in order to get the serial #. Nowhere did the claim say anything about needing to purchase multiple appliances to be eligible. Only after submitting the form was I informed that I was not eligible (no details as to why). After literally hours on hold waiting to talk with support I was finally told the reason. I am very disappointed about this false advertising and am sorely tempted to contact the better business bureau to file a complaint. Needless to say, I doubt that I will be giving much future business to either Lowes or Bosch and I certainly will advise friends and other colleagues to be very wary of rebate offers that seem to good to be true!

Sentence (English): I really wanted to love this dishwasher as it was the last piece of a matching Bosch kitchen.
Comments (English): [ Too many tines and in all the wrong places. ] || ---------------- || I really wanted to love this dishwasher as it was the last piece of a matching Bosch kitchen. But there is one glaring problem: it has too many tines, too close together, and at funky angles. This setup, I assume, is perfect for a family that uses lots of large plates, but few mugs, bowls, pint-glasses, wine-glasses, etc. Not us. Oh, not just lots of tines but (on the lower rack) almost no horizontal bars either so big bowls don't really fit unless tipped over. The good news is that the upper rack can be lowered and while the tines there are weird, at least I have a place for big coffee mugs, etc. The attached picture is a random snapshot, but basically shows the problem. Upper shelf is packed. Lower shelf is empty because nothing else will fit.This means we now do 2 washes a day whereas we did one previously, which gets me to my next peeve: there is no way of knowing if the dishwasher has run. Most dishwashers have an LED or something to indicate completion whereas this dishwasher just goes silent to indicate completion. This is annoying mistake for an expensive dishwasher. Cleaning efficiency is average. Seems not uncommon to find a stained spoon or something. Note that I do not, in the slightest, wash anything before it goes into the machine, so maybe that is my fault.The good (almost bad! ) news is that the dishwasher is amazingly silent. So easy, in fact, for half the family to assume that it has never even been turned on. It has a light shining down to the floor when the dishwasher is active, but my kids seem to always ignore that and open the door anyway. Not really Bosch's fault! This gets me to completely irrelevant detail, but still somewhat irritating. If ever you find that you need to cancel a run, then the Bosch instructions say "hold the Cancel button for 5 seconds". There is no Cancel button. Only a "Start/Resume" button. but yes, holding the "Start" button is indeed how to cancel. Now we know.One other problem is likely my fault because I haven't called Best Buy to come and fix it yet, but "Start" doesn't work, at least not by itself. You have to hold the Reset button for 5 seconds and [only] then does the Start button work to initiate the dishwasher cycle. It also seems to get confused if ever the main power supply is turned off, so we always leave it powered on now.The combination of software/electrical issues and high price drops my rating from 5 stars to 4. But not being able to really load up the dishwasher gets me to a 3 - it puts me in a bad mood whenever I load the dishes.

But there is one glaring problem: it has too many tines, too close together, and at funky angles. This setup, I assume, is perfect for a family that uses lots of large plates, but few mugs, bowls, pint-glasses, wine-glasses, etc. Not us. Oh, not just lots of tines but (on the lower rack) almost no horizontal bars either so big bowls don't really fit unless tipped over. The good news is that the upper rack can be lowered and while the tines there are weird, at least I have a place for big coffee mugs, etc. The attached picture is a random snapshot, but basically shows the problem. Upper shelf is packed. Lower shelf is empty because nothing else will fit.This means we now do 2 washes a day whereas we did one previously, which gets me to my next peeve: there is no way of knowing if the dishwasher has run. Most dishwashers have an LED or something to indicate completion whereas this dishwasher just goes silent to indicate completion. This is annoying mistake for an expensive dishwasher. Cleaning efficiency is average. Seems not uncommon to find a stained spoon or something. Note that I do not, in the slightest, wash anything before it goes into the machine, so maybe that is my fault.The good (almost bad! ) news is that the dishwasher is amazingly silent. So easy, in fact, for half the family to assume that it has never even been turned on. It has a light shining down to the floor when the dishwasher is active, but my kids seem to always ignore that and open the door anyway. Not really Bosch's fault! This gets me to completely irrelevant detail, but still somewhat irritating. If ever you find that you need to cancel a run, then the Bosch instructions say "hold the Cancel button for 5 seconds". There is no Cancel button. Only a "Start/Resume" button. but yes, holding the "Start" button is indeed how to cancel. Now we know.One other problem is likely my fault because I haven't called Best Buy to come and fix it yet, but "Start" doesn't work, at least not by itself. You have to hold the Reset button for 5 seconds and [only] then does the Start button work to initiate the dishwasher cycle. It also seems to get confused if ever the main power supply is turned off, so we always leave it powered on now.The combination of software/electrical issues and high price drops my rating from 5 stars to 4. But not being able to really load up the dishwasher gets me to a 3 - it puts me in a bad mood whenever I load the dishes.

I'm now doing dishes by hand for a family of 6-- and hauling this thing to the dump where it belongs. Seriously run away. You do not want this machine!

Sentence (English): I'm finally satisfied with my LG dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ I'm finally satisfied with the LG dishwasher I bought. ] || ---------------- || I'm finally satisfied with my LG dishwasher. I've wanted to buy one since the day I moved in four years ago, but I kept putting it off because of the lack of space and the idea of having to restore the dishwasher to its original location after moving. It was a foolish thought. I decided I couldn't put it off any longer, and once I decided to buy a dishwasher, it magically became a reality. I don't know why I kept worrying about it. The lack of space was solved by repurposing the empty drawer I had to install the dishwasher into and placing it opposite. Because our kitchen is small, we only had one spot for the dishwasher: under the induction stove. The biggest problem was not being able to remove the drawer. But now that I can use the removed drawer across from it, that problem is solved! Second, if I move, I can put the repurposed drawer back in, and if the next person uses the dishwasher, it's safe to move. This problem was easily solved by simply leaving it empty. After using the dishwasher for almost a month, I've noticed that it doesn't dramatically reduce the amount of dishes I wash. However, it's better than nothing, and I feel like my dishes are cleaner. I tend to have a hard time loading dirty dishes, so even after pre-loading, I didn't notice a significant reduction in dishes. At first, I was a bit unfamiliar with dish storage, so it took a bit longer. I chose the basic model, which offers a reasonable price and doesn't come with high specs. The 80-degree water wash seemed sufficient, and the high-temperature hot air mode is also a nice feature, so I thought the basic model would be sufficient. While higher-spec models do dry faster and feel better, if you don't want to spend a lot, I recommend the basic model for a more cost-effective price. I used to collect the dishes from breakfast and lunch and then run them, but my house is too small for that, and I didn't like leaving dirty dishes all day, so I've developed a routine. I do small amounts of dishes right away. If I cook dinner and have a lot of dishes, I use the dishwasher without overdoing it. If I turn off the dryer and wash on standard mode, it takes about 50 minutes to finish.
